QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_11

question.text: Aravalli Long-Short posted sub-period returns of +5%, -2%, +8%, +3% in four consecutive quarters. What is the annual Time-Weighted Return (TWR) for the year?

explanation.text: The Logic: Time-Weighted Return is computed by linking the sub-period returns geometrically: TWR = (1 + r1) × (1 + r2) × (1 + r3) × (1 + r4) − 1. With quarterly returns of +5%, -2%, +8%, +3%, that is (1.05) × (0.98) × (1.08) × (1.03) − 1 = 1.14448... − 1 ≈ 14.45%. TWR is the standard methodology used to express manager performance independent of investor cash flows. The Trap: 14.00% is the simple arithmetic sum (5 − 2 + 8 + 3). 3.50% is the arithmetic average of the four sub-period returns. 14.55% reflects a rounding/compounding error rather than the correct geometric link. Note: The cited NISM Series XIX-E workbook page (156) lists Time-weighted Rate of Return as a GIPS calculation methodology but does not give the geometric-linking formula or a worked example with quarterly compounding. The TWR formula above is general industry/regulatory knowledge as codified by GIPS, rather than a workbook-page citation.
